title: Pre-Authentication SSL VPN Request Validation and Parser Shielding
description: Synthetic evaluation of whether a pre-parser validation layer can reject structurally invalid VPN-like requests before they reach sensitive processing, modeled on pre-authentication SSL VPN request-handling weaknesses.

related_cves.trust_boundary: Internet to pre-auth SSL VPN service
related_cves.vendor_mitigation: Upgrade to fixed FortiOS versions per FG-IR-24-015 (7.4.3, 7.2.7, 7.0.14, 6.4.15, 6.2.16+); workaround: disable SSL VPN.
related_cves.mitigation_gap: Patch only / operational recovery unspecified: fixed versions and the disable-SSL-VPN workaround are clear, but the advisory gives limited guidance on post-compromise credential rotation and persistence hunting.

failure_pattern: Internet-facing SSL VPN service automatically parses attacker-controlled HTTP/TLS request data before authentication, allowing malformed or oversized fields to reach memory-unsafe or under-validated processing code.
vendor_mitigation: Vendor-issued firmware/software upgrade to a fixed release, with SSL VPN disablement offered as an interim workaround.
mitigation_gap: Patch availability does not by itself prove session or credential hygiene, or that persistence was addressed after exposure.
research_question: Can a pre-parser validation layer reject structurally invalid VPN-like requests before sensitive processing?
hypothesis: A strict schema, length, type, duplicate-field, and canonicalisation validation layer will reject a materially higher proportion of malformed synthetic VPN-like requests than a weak baseline, while preserving acceptance of valid requests.
